entry.title:
[vahidkarimipour] A word to students
After the letter from 46 professors of Sharif University of…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

A word to students

After the letter from 46 professors of Sharif University of Technology titled "For Sharif" was sent—which was in fact these colleagues' response to the "Letter from the Mothers of Students Expelled from Sharif"—I and at least four other colleagues who, unfortunately, did not have the honor of writing that letter but had signed it, received numerous messages from some students. All of them, while maintaining a polite tone, asked: "What was your feeling as signatories of this letter when the attack on Minab school happened?" and "Why did these professors not issue a statement at that time and condemn it?" This text is a response to those students.

The attack on Minab school and the killing of innocent children is undoubtedly a war crime. I hope that after the war ends, it will be pursued through an official complaint filed by the government and that appropriate compensation will be granted to the victims' families, although receiving compensation will never bring those innocent children back to their families' arms nor cool that eternal grief.

Therefore, the right way to deal with such atrocities is to pursue them through governmental and international institutions, not to have them condemned by this or that group of citizens. If the professors' letter had merely condemned the expulsion of students, it would have been a useless act as well. Instead, this letter contains a specific demand from the university president to review these rulings in accordance with revised procedures.

And now a word to the students who are dissatisfied with this letter and still support the expulsion of a group of their classmates. In my opinion, in any country in the world, the human and moral duty of a citizen is to side with a fellow citizen when they are up against organizations and institutions, to listen to their words, and to demand fair treatment for them, rather than siding with that organization or institution. The reason is very simple: because even an organization like the municipality is powerful enough and, when facing a citizen, does not need the support of another citizen. Even if a student lives in the most democratic country in the world, when it comes to a student versus an organization, ethically one should stand by one's classmate, not by that organization. For a student, being on a committee where another student—their classmate—receives an expulsion ruling is never a commendable act, and perhaps years later, when the fervor of youth subsides, it will bring shame and regret.

entry.title: [vahidkarimipour] The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at Sharif University of Technology to one of our colleagues, and in fact to the entire body of colleagues at Sharif University of Technology. Its audience is, in reality, all professors and officials of Iranian universities.——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————-We are a group of mothers whose children have, in recent months, faced heavy disciplinary rulings and expulsion from university. We write this letter not out of confrontation, nor to disregard the rules, but from the position of mothers who are worried about the future, the fate, and the lost years of youth of their children, and we have turned to you with great hope. Our children may have made mistakes or committed violations under certain circumstances, and it is natural that the university has the right to react to violations; but is taking away the opportunity to continue education and destroying the future path of a young person the only possible response to a mistake? What pains us most of all is the severity and sometimes irreparability of the punishment that affects the future of these young people. Many of these students have strived for years to get into Sharif University, have completed a significant portion of their studies, and their families have placed all their hope and resources into their future. What is most painful for us is that some of these students, in addition to the disciplinary case at the university and the expulsion ruling, have also faced punishment from the judicial system (mostly one to three years of imprisonment); that is, for a single offense at the university, they have faced two punishments from two institutions—the university and the judicial system! We ask you, if possible, to hear the voice of these mothers and, to the extent of your ability, help in reviewing the expulsion rulings, converting heavy punishments into more proportionate rulings, and providing the possibility for these students to return to the path of education. Sometimes a second chance can save a young person's life. We do not expect you to disregard the law; we only ask that alongside the law, fairness, proportionality of punishment, the circumstances of each student, and the future of a human being also be considered. If you have the means to follow up on these concerns or convey them to university officials or officials of the Ministry of Science, we sincerely request that you do not leave us alone. We thank you in advance for the time you take to hear our voice. With respect and hope, a group of mothers of expelled students of Sharif University of Technology
